title: Are Display Ad Content and Landing Page Ad Content Complements or Substitutes? A Field Experiment
affiliations: Stanford Graduate School of Business and Santa Clara University

detail.title: Are Display Ad Content and Landing Page Ad Content Complements or Substitutes? A Field Experiment
detail.abstract: We study whether sequential ad content - display ads and landing page ads - act as substitutes or complements using a field experiment with a semiconductor firm. Ad headlines emphasizing product quality or transactional ease were randomly assigned across two ad placements in eight markets. Using pre-experiment organic traffic to infer prior knowledge about the advertised products, we find that the relationship between the two contents varies with prior information. In low-information markets, two quality-focused contents across placements showed substitutability, consistent with ad content serving as a source of information. In high-information markets, they exhibited complementarity, suggesting their preference-matching role. Decomposing quality-focused content reveals that content emphasizing horizontal match drives information provision, whereas content highlighting vertical quality supports preference matching. Our findings suggest that even coarse, market-level coordination of sequential ad content substantially improves online customer acquisition-lowering cost per action by 37.7%.

title: Market as a Machine (M²): A Trust-First Control Loop for Modern Markets

detail.title: Market as a Machine (M²): A Trust-First Control Loop for Modern Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported. The author is the founder of the M² Educational Initiative (pre-launch) and Anahila Research & Consulting; these entities did not provide funding and had no role in the analysis or conclusions.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual/theoretical study with no experiments, human participants, animals, or identifiable personal data; therefore ethics approval was not required. The illustrative vignettes are anonymized composites for explanatory purposes only.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding. The research was self-funded by the author (time and resources).

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Market as a Machine (M²) framework, modeling markets as self-regulating feedback systems rather than unpredictable or purely linear spaces. Grounded in systems engineering, behavioral economics, and organizational learning, the M² Method treats marketing and sales as a closed-loop system: Signals (S)-the messages you send; Processing (Π)-how your organization interprets signals and feedback; Behavior/Output (B)-how customers respond; and Feedback (F)what you capture and learn. At the center is Trust (T ∈ [0,1]), a measurable state you can monitor and manage. We adapt familiar engineering ideas-friction (extra effort), delay (slow response), damping (reducing swings), and stability (keeping things steady)-to business decisions, and offer four tools leaders can apply immediately: (1) Trust Path Mapping, (2) a Signal Directory, (3) a Concession Matrix for principled negotiation, and (4) Post-mortem & Failure Analysis. Leaders can start by measuring Trust, mapping which signals move it, and setting simple guardrails to keep operations stable. We include key metrics, safety checks, and templates that show practical effects on user experience, sales routines, and pricing in unstable markets.

title: Hospital Community Benefit Regulations and Consumer Financial Health
affiliations: University of Virginia - Darden School of Business and University of Virginia - Darden School of Business

detail.title: Hospital Community Benefit Regulations and Consumer Financial Health
detail.abstract: To preserve their tax-exempt status, nonprofit hospitals must meet the Community Benefits Requirements (CBR) that impose significant restrictions on nonprofit hospitals' financial assistance, billing, and collection practices. For-profit hospitals are exempt from these requirements. We show that financially vulnerable consumers, those most positioned to benefit from CBR, default significantly more if they reside in localities served by for-profit hospitals. These effects are amplified in states with more stringent CBR requirements. Yet these effects are attenuated in states that uniformly regulate all hospitals' financial assistance, billing, and collection practices. These effects affect the geographic distribution of hospitals. For-profit hospitals, not bound by CBRs, have a higher presence in communities where CBR pressures on nonprofit hospitals are most costly: those characterized by lower income, lower credit score, and higher debtto-income ratio consumers. The last results illustrate the potential unintended consequences of the CBRs as they contribute to for-profit hospitals serving financially vulnerable consumers who are in need of CBR-driven financial assistance.

title: Efficient Project Management in Sustainable Urban Development: A Case Study of Balancing Green Spaces, Urban Density, and Community Needs
affiliations: Oxford Academy and George Mason University

detail.title: Efficient Project Management in Sustainable Urban Development: A Case Study of Balancing Green Spaces, Urban Density, and Community Needs
detail.abstract: Urban development in the twenty-first century is defined by the dual challenge of promoting spatial efficiency through higher density while preserving environmental quality and community wellbeing through accessible green infrastructure. This thesis explores how project management strategies can be effectively adapted to reconcile these competing priorities within the sustainable urban development agenda of developing countries. Employing a mixed-method research design, the study integrates quantitative surveys from residents and stakeholders with qualitative interviews, project documentation reviews, and expert consultations. This methodological triangulation provides a comprehensive understanding of how project governance, stakeholder participation, and sustainability metrics intersect in contemporary urban development projects. The findings reveal that the most efficient urban projects in developing contexts succeed through four core enablers: (1) inclusive stakeholder governance; (2) adaptive project planning that embeds environmental considerations from inception; (3) community-driven performance evaluation frameworks; and (4) institutional capacity-building for integrated urban management. Conversely, fragmented governance, political inconsistency, and the absence of long-term maintenance planning are identified as recurrent barriers. Building on these insights, the thesis proposes the Integrated Sustainable Urban Project Management Framework (ISUPMF)-a practical model aligning project lifecycle management with urban sustainability objectives. The framework bridges theory and practice, offering policymakers, urban planners, and project managers a roadmap for delivering projects that optimise density, preserve ecological assets, and respond to community needs. This research contributes to academic and professional discourse by contextualising project management within sustainable urban development for developing economies. It underscores the principle that sustainability is not achieved solely through design or technology but through efficient, inclusive, and adaptive project management that harmonises people, place, and performance.

title: Dependencies :Pakistan–Saudi Relations and the 2025 SMDA

detail.title: Dependencies :Pakistan–Saudi Relations and the 2025 SMDA
detail.abstract: The Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (SMDA) signed between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on 17 September 2025 represents the latest iteration of a decades-long, asymmetrical security relationship. Rooted in Cold War-era collaborations and shaped by transactional defense arrangements, the bilateral partnership has historically favored Saudi strategic imperatives, with Pakistan providing military manpower, training, and, potentially, nuclear assurances. While Islamabad frames the SMDA as a shield against Indian military threats, Riyadh’s priorities are centered on regional security challenges, particularly Iran and its proxies. Historical patterns—from deployments during the Gulf War to post-9/11 counterterrorism realignments—illustrate recurring asymmetries in obligations and benefits. The 2025 SMDA formalizes collective defense language but risks exposing Pakistan to economic and geopolitical vulnerabilities, including dependency, limited strategic autonomy, and potential sanctions. This study situates the agreement within the broader trajectory of Pakistan–Saudi relations, highlighting structural imbalances, regional implications, and the interplay of economic, military, and nuclear dimensions.

title: Beneficiation Vs. Knowledge-Based: Dead Ends and Steppingstones to Productive Diversification
affiliations: Harvard University and Instituto Tecnologico y de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey - Escuela de Gobierno y Transformación Pública

detail.title: Beneficiation Vs. Knowledge-Based: Dead Ends and Steppingstones to Productive Diversification

publicationDetails.detailsText: The paper has been submitted to a journal and is in the process of peer reviewed

detail.abstract: The global resurgence of industrial policy has revived the appeal of downstream diversification (beneficiation)-adding value to raw materials-as a development strategy. Despite this intuitive appeal, empirical evidence of its effectiveness remains scarce, with few real-world success stories. We address this gap through a novel empirical analysis of export product co-location and new relatedness metrics to explain observed diversification patterns. Our results show that product co-location patterns are driven primarily by similarities in occupational structures. Industries sharing high-skill occupations (and to a lesser extent, non-tradable inputs) are strong predictors of diversification. Conversely, relatedness metrics based on value-chain linkages (existing upstream inputs) have weak to no predictive power. These findings suggest rethinking development strategies focused on adding value to raw materials. Instead, countries should promote industries that build on existing know-how-particularly those with similar occupational structures or non-tradable capabilities already present in the economy.

title: Two cross-species Drivers of Fertility

detail.title: Two cross-species Drivers of Fertility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. This research was conducted independently with no personal, financial, or institutional relationships that could be perceived to influence the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involves no human participants, animals, or identifiable personal data; it is a theoretical/synthesis paper using publicly available information. Therefore, ethics approval and informed consent were not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this work. The study was self-initiated and self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: When should life reproduce? Existing theories fail to unify reproductive timing across kingdoms and often misapply species-level r/K selection to individual decisions. We propose a universal P-T-C principle: all multicellular organisms exhibit one of three reproductive states-Programmed (P), Threat-triggered (T), or Competition-delayed (C). In safe environments, individuals follow intrinsic developmental programs (P); under survival threat, they accelerate reproduction (T); under intense competition, they delay reproduction to avoid elimination (C). This framework is supported across plants, insects, mammals, and humans. Crucially, it resolves long-standing conceptual confusion by separating analytical scales: r/K describes interspecific evolutionary strategies, while P-T-C governs intraspecific state switching-providing a unified, cross-kingdom foundation for understanding fertility dynamics from ecology to society.

title: Does Transparency of a Firm's AI Models Decrease its Profits?
affiliations: Yeshiva University - Syms School of Business

detail.title: Does Transparency of a Firm's AI Models Decrease its Profits?

declarations.funderStatement: YU Sy Syms Dean’s Research Fund.

detail.abstract: This paper models the relationship between the transparency of a prominent firm’s AI technology and its financial performance. Users adopting the firm’s AI provide data, the technology’s key input. I show that, under rational expectations, the firm benefits from making the technology less transparent to users in some cases. Although reduced transparency lowers adoption and data collection, it curbs excess spending. The lack of transparency does not depend on competition or legal risks, but on the firm's incentives to impress investors. Lack of transparency is thus inherent to technology development. However, funding alternatives in addition to financial markets could motivate the firm to increase transparency.

reference: African Journal of International and Comparative Law (Forthcoming, 2025)
title: The Danger of a Single Story: Revisiting the History and Evolution of Fintech

detail.title: The Danger of a Single Story: Revisiting the History and Evolution of Fintech

publicationDetails.detailsText: African Journal of International and Comparative Law (Forthcoming, 2025)

detail.abstract: The dominant narrative within the literature on the history and evolution of fintech is inordinately western-centric as it is centred around the experience in Europe and the United States. This article proposes a nuanced approach to analysing the history of fintech beyond the perspectives of developed countries. It explores the application of technology to finance within the context of the prevailing socioeconomic and political landscape in several African countries during the pre-colonial, colonial and post-colonial era respectively. The article argues that failure to properly situate the peculiarities of the African fintech story in the literature, including the factors that have defined the African experience, has undermined the design of effective fintech regulations on the continent. Consequently, the prevailing regulatory environment for fintech in several African countries promotes some exploitative fintech products that are inimical to the interests of Africans. To harness the potentials that fintech presents for African countries, financial regulators need to learn from history.

title: Impact of Application's Embeddedness in the Integration Network on Product Market Penetration
affiliations: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology and Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Impact of Application's Embeddedness in the Integration Network on Product Market Penetration
detail.abstract: With the rise of super-apps, the innovation model of apps is shifting from singular technological breakthroughs to cross-scenario collaborative integration. However, this shift has led to a crisis of user trust and loss of market share under the systemic security risks arising from integration. Grounded in Information Ecology and Niche Theory, this study investigates how apps within a platform ecosystem influence market penetration through their integration network embeddings and the underlying mechanisms. Utilizing Python to scrape sample data comprising 1,604 apps from the HubSpot platform, the research reveals that: (1) A higher degree of integration network embedding of an app leads to better market penetration; (2) Niche breadth positively moderates the relationship between an app's degree of integration network embedding and its market penetration; (3) Data sharing mediates the relationship between an app's degree of integration network embedding and its market penetration. This study not only expands the theoretical explanatory boundaries in the context of digital platform ecosystems but also provides a decision-making basis for third-party enterprises to optimize their technology collaboration strategies and data asset allocation.

title: Digital Banking and Youth Engagement in the Contemporary World: Analyzing Popularity, Usage Patterns, and Satisfaction Drivers among Millennials and Gen-Z

detail.title: Digital Banking and Youth Engagement in the Contemporary World: Analyzing Popularity, Usage Patterns, and Satisfaction Drivers among Millennials and Gen-Z
detail.abstract: The research explores the participation of the Millennials and the Generation Z in digital banking in list of its popularity, its usage rates as well as the drivers of its satisfaction in the context of business analytics. The objective is to explore the disparities within the generations in respect of experiencing electronic banking and the effect of predictive analytics, individualization and safety on interaction and dedication. The mixed-method orientation uses secondary data. The thematic coding factors reveals the following factors of adoption i.e., ease of use, personalization, trust, cost-effectiveness and the innovation factor, the trend analysis identifies the rate of adoption, the number of engagements and the amount of satisfactory in the two cohorts. The finding reported above shows that Millennials consider usability, reliability and financial planning tools more important; and mobiles-first banking experience, gamification, and social alignment are among Gen Z.

title: Strategic Optimization of "Buy One on the Way" Recommendations and Pricing in Competitive E-commerce

detail.title: Strategic Optimization of "Buy One on the Way" Recommendations and Pricing in Competitive E-commerce
detail.abstract: In e-commerce platforms, checkout recommendations such as "Buy One on the Way" (BOW) have emerged as a powerful strategy that leverages a consumer's primary purchase to boost overall profitability. However, existing research primarily focuses on recommendation accuracy, overlooking the interplay with pricing strategies and consumer dissatisfaction. This study introduces a novel BOW optimization model for competitive platforms, aiming to maximize profits while accounting for disappointment utility. The model is formulated within a game-theoretic framework. Two analytical approaches are developed: first, by categorizing competition into three adoption scenarios—non-adoption, asymmetric adoption, and full adoption to derive optimal pricing and strategy decisions; and second, by analyzing equilibrium choices for product categories. The findings suggest that platforms with a recommendation accuracy advantage can increase profits through strategic BOW pricing. In contrast, platforms with lower accuracy must adopt BOW defensively once competitors’ recommendation quality surpasses a critical threshold. Furthermore, complementary product recommendations can enhance conversion rates, but only when the benefits of facilitating the recommendation process outweigh the technical matching challenges. This paper also provides managerial insights on how to effectively implement BOW strategiesIn e-commerce platforms, checkout recommendations such as "Buy One on the Way" (BOW) have emerged as a powerful strategy that leverages a consumer's primary purchase to boost overall profitability. title: A Path to Increased Representation of Top 10% and Minority Students in Texas College Admission
affiliations: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals, North Carolina State University and University of Alabama

detail.title: A Path to Increased Representation of Top 10% and Minority Students in Texas College Admission
detail.abstract: We study the effects of precedence order (i.e., the order in which different types of seats are filled) on college admission under the Texas Top 10% Law, which requires automatic admission for any student who graduated in the top 10% from a Texas high school. Policymakers currently fill reserved seats for top 10% students first, then fill unreserved seats. Using publicly available data, we show that the reserve policy with the current precedence order is equivalent to admission without reserves. We show that switching the precedence order to fill unreserved seats first increases the admission rates for top 10% students and for Black and Hispanic students. By filling unreserved seats before reserved seats, policymakers could increase the representation of racial/ethnic minorities at highly selective colleges.

title: Effect of Cheap Talk in an Asymmetric Contest: An Experimental Investigation
affiliations: Jawaharlal Nehru University - Centre for Economic Studies and Planning (CESP) and Jawaharlal Nehru University

detail.title: Effect of Cheap Talk in an Asymmetric Contest: An Experimental Investigation
detail.abstract: This paper experimentally investigates the effect of pre-play cheap talk communication on bidding behavior in asymmetric Tullock contests with one-sided incomplete information. We implement a 2×2 design that varies information structure (complete vs. one-sided asymmetric information) and the availability of non-binding communication. Our results reveal significant and persistent overbidding across all treatments, with efforts substantially exceeding theoretical Nash predictions, particularly under one-sided asymmetry. We find that cheap talk has a conditional effect: it significantly reduces average effort levels in environments with incomplete information, especially in contests between high-and low-type players, yet it simultaneously increases the variance of efforts. However, communication yields negligible effects in complete information settings. Furthermore, analysis of player beliefs indicates systematic over-contribution relative to beliefs about opponents' efforts. Our mediation analysis rules out emotional pathways as a mechanism for treatment effects. These results demonstrate that cheap talk serves as an effective coordination device for mitigating overbidding under asymmetric information, with important implications for the design of contests and competitive mechanisms.

title: Risk on the Run: Public Pension Underfunding with Migration Risk
affiliations: University of Chicago Booth School of Business

detail.title: Risk on the Run: Public Pension Underfunding with Migration Risk
detail.abstract: How does local debt sustain with a mobile tax-base? This paper provides new evidence on how pension underfunding shapes inter-state migration. Exploiting plausibly exogenous variation in funding gaps driven by relative portfolio performance, I find that widening pension deficits significantly increase net out-migration of households and income flows from underfunded to better-funded states. This mobility erodes the tax base, raising the effective cost of funding pensions and constraining governments’ ability to close shortfalls through higher contributions. I further show that states facing higher “migration risk”—those that face larger out-migration when local taxes rise—systematically under-contribute relative to actuarially required levels and shift pension assets toward opaque, higher-yielding alternatives such as private equity and hedge funds. This pattern reveals a novel mechanism by which household mobility exacerbates both fiscal fragility and risk-taking incentives. To interpret these findings, I develop a spatial model of tax-setting and pension investment under endogenous migration. The model highlights a migration–funding–risk feedback loop: governments that fail to internalize out-migration overestimate tax capacity, under-contribute, and induce fiduciaries to pursue riskier portfolios.

title: Labor Market Frictions and Asset Prices
affiliations: INSEAD, University of British Columbia (UBC) - Division of Finance and University of Minnesota

detail.title: Labor Market Frictions and Asset Prices
detail.abstract: We survey research on labor market frictions and their implications for asset pricing. Starting from a neoclassical, frictionless labor model as the benchmark, we introduce labor adjustment costs and wage rigidity to examine how these frictions shape firm value, risk, and expected returns. Labor adjustment costs make a firm's installed labor force a quasi-fixed asset that directly contributes to valuation, while wage rigidity acts as operating leverage, amplifying profit volatility and raising required returns. The interaction between labor and financial frictions magnifies these effects, as labor commitments constrain financial flexibility and heighten default risk. We then consider extensions incorporating labor heterogeneity, capital-skill complementarity, task automation, search-and-matching frictions, and imperfect risk sharing between firms and workers. For each framework, we review the related theoretical mechanisms and supporting empirical evidence. Overall, labor market frictions play a central role in determining firm valuations and risk exposures.

title: Drowning in Waste: A Critique of the Plastic Island

detail.title: Drowning in Waste: A Critique of the Plastic Island
detail.abstract:
What happens when a paradise of clear blue waters and golden sands turns into a floating sea of garbage? Indonesia, a nation celebrated for its natural beauty, is now drowning in plastic waste a crisis that threatens both its environment and its people.
Plastic Island (Pulau Plastik), a 2021 Netflix documentary directed by Dandhy Laksono and Rahung Nasution, confronts this environmental catastrophe head-on. It follows three Indonesian advocates Gede Robi, a musician and activist; Tiza Mafira, a lawyer focused on environmental policy; and Prigi Arisandi, a biologist and river guardian. Together, they embark on a journey across Indonesia to trace the origins, consequences, and solutions to plastic pollution that now plagues their homeland.
Through a mix of emotional storytelling, factual investigation, and striking imagery, Plastic Island exposes plastic pollution as not just an ecological threat but also a social and ethical challenge that requires urgent global attention.

title: China's 2024 Economic Stimulus

detail.title: China's 2024 Economic Stimulus
detail.abstract: This study reviews China's largest post-COVID economic stimulus launched in September-October 2024, examining its background, policy contents, early effects, and broader implications. Specifically, triggered by worsening economic conditions, the package aimed to stabilize stock and real estate markets, support consumption, and ease local financial stress while continuing strategic hi-tech development. By March 2025, results were mixed-weak demand persisted, but favoured sectors showed gains. This case illustrates China's balancing act between short-term fixes and long-term ambitions, development and security, and reflects growing state intervention in the economy. It offers insights for understanding China's evolving policy logic and navigating debates on its future trajectory, including the "peak China" discourse.

title: Issuance Overpricing in Chinese Corporate Bond Market: The Role of Shadow Investors
affiliations: , , Buzhou Mountain (Jilin) Information Technology Consulting Services Co., Ltd and Macquarie University

detail.title: Issuance Overpricing in Chinese Corporate Bond Market: The Role of Shadow Investors
detail.abstract: This study reveals how shadow investors distort bond issuance prices in China's exchange bond market. We developed a novel metric to detect the presence of shadow investors in bond issuance. By exploiting different extent of shadow investors' participation in public-and private-placed bond issuance and exogenous policy shocks targeting structured issuance, we identify a significant causal relationship between shadow investors' involvement and bond overpricing. Additionally, we find that tightened regulations on structured issuance in the public bond market inadvertently increased overpricing in the private-placed bond market by pushing shadow investors there. Cross-sectional analyses further demonstrate that shadow investors have a more pronounced impact on bonds issued by local state-owned enterprises (including LGFVs) and firms with lower credit ratings. Overall, we document the participation of shadow investors as an important mechanism in understanding the unique overpricing phenomenon for China's corporate bond issuance.

title: The Impact of Cash Flow on Dividend Payment Decisions in Multinational Corporations Listed on the Rwanda Stock Exchange
affiliations: Lincoln University College, Malaysia and Lincoln University College, Malaysia

detail.title: The Impact of Cash Flow on Dividend Payment Decisions in Multinational Corporations Listed on the Rwanda Stock Exchange

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. The research was conducted independently for academic purposes, and all analyses and interpretations are solely those of the authors. None of the authors has any affiliation, financial interest, or other connection with any organization or entity that has a direct or indirect interest in the subject matter discussed in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based exclusively on publicly available secondary financial data of firms listed on the Rwanda Stock Exchange and does not involve human participants, animals, or confidential data. Therefore, formal ethical approval was not required under institutional research guidelines. The authors confirm that all data sources were appropriately cited, and the research complies with principles of academic integrity, transparency, and responsible scholarship.

The study was fully supported by the authors’ institutional affiliation, Lincoln University College, Selangor, Malaysia, through access to research resources and academic supervision. All research expenses were personally covered by the authors.

detail.abstract: This study examines how different cash flow types (operating, investing, financing) influence dividend payout decisions in multinational companies listed on the Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE) over 2015-2024. Drawing on dividend theories (signaling, agency, pecking order), we use a quantitative panel-data approach. Annual financial data for RSE-listed firms were collected and a panel regression model was estimated with dividend payout ratio as the dependent variable and cash flow components plus controls (profitability, firm size, leverage) as independents. Results indicate that operating cash flow (OCF) has a significant positive effect on dividends, while heavy investing cash flows (net investment outflows) tend to reduce dividends. Financing cash flows (raising capital) showed no statistically significant impact. The findings align with theory: dividends are typically paid from stable operational cash (consistent with pecking order and Lintner models), and large investment outlays crowd out payouts. The study contributes new evidence from Rwanda, highlighting that managers should align investment and dividend plans Limitations include the small market sample and potential omitted factors. For financial managers, the implication is clear: robust operational cash generation is crucial to sustain dividends, and large capital expenditures should be communicated as trade-offs for dividend levels. Policymakers and regulators should ensure transparent reporting of cash flows to support market confidence.

title: Dependence-Preserving Simulation for Retirement Planning: Evidence from Indian Financial Markets

detail.title: Dependence-Preserving Simulation for Retirement Planning: Evidence from Indian Financial Markets
detail.abstract: Conventional Monte Carlo retirement simulations assume independent, identically distributed returns-an assumption violated in markets where interest rates are cyclical and equity volatility clusters. Using Indian post-liberalisation data (1992-2025), we show that this simplification understates retirement failure probability by 50-170 basis points relative to a dependencepreserving circular block bootstrap, with bias increasing linearly in equity exposure. Fixeddeposit rates exhibit strong annual autocorrelation (ACF 12 = 0.41) and equity-deposit correlations intensify in crises. Conventional iteration counts (N < 10,000) produce confidence intervals two to three times wider than target precision and fail to detect this bias in up to half of tests. Robust inference requires 35,000-100,000 iterations-computationally trivial today. Therefore, dependence preservation and adequate iteration size are essential for a defensible assessment of tail risks and accurate estimates of safe withdrawal in India.

reference: Bank of England Macro Technical Paper No. 5
title: Monetary Policymaking under Uncertainty
affiliations: Bank of England, Bank of England - Monetary Analysis, Bank of England - Monetary Analysis and Bank of England

detail.title: Monetary Policymaking under Uncertainty

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of England Macro Technical Paper No. 5

detail.abstract: Pervasive and time-varying uncertainty characterises the monetary policy environment. While theory provides insights into setting monetary policy under uncertainty, it is widely recognised that theoretical approaches are too simplified to be directly applicable. This paper discusses three alternative perspectives on the policy problem that can be applied in practice and that acknowledge uncertainty in different ways: a forecast-based, a news‑based, and a rules‑based perspective. These perspectives are complementary so that insights from all of them may be informative for policymaking. They should also be applied flexibly and with varying emphases depending on judgements about the prevailing level and nature of uncertainty. These observations provide some context for the approach that the Bank of England is taking to adapting monetary policymaking as part of its response to the Bernanke Review.

title: A Flexible Framework for Estimating the Monthly Discount Factor (β)
affiliations: University of Colorado at Denver - Department of Finance

detail.title: A Flexible Framework for Estimating the Monthly Discount Factor (β)
detail.abstract: We develop a flexible econometric framework to estimate the monthly representative-agent discount factor (𝛽 𝑡) under CRRA and Epstein-Zin (EZ) preferences. Using U.S. data on consumption growth, risk-free returns, and market performance (1963-2025), we first identify risk aversion (𝛾) and the elasticity of intertemporal substitution (EIS) via log-linearized Euler equations, then construct a high-frequency series of 𝛽 𝑡. Comparing the two, 𝛽 𝐶𝑅𝑅𝐴 and 𝛽 𝐸𝑍 are highly correlated but not interchangeable; the CRRA series is a smoother, upward-shifted version of the EZ series. The estimated 𝛽 𝑡 averages about 0.997 is highly persistent and shows pronounced but temporary movements during major disruptions (e.g., COVID-19). Macroeconomically, 𝛽 𝑡 rises with inflation and falls with higher policy rates, indicating greater household patience in inflationary or low-rate environments. Extending the analysis to the cross-section of 49 Fama-French sectors, a Fama-MacBeth framework shows that innovations in𝛽 𝑡 , interpreted as patience shocks, are positively and significantly associated with sectoral volatility. These findings indicate that time-preference dynamics shape intertemporal decisions and act as a state variable for market uncertainty, with implications for monetary policy, asset pricing, and macro-financial stability.

title: Pricing Options on Assets with Negative Prices using Simple Models

detail.title: Pricing Options on Assets with Negative Prices using Simple Models
detail.abstract: The original Black-Scholes paper is based on geometric Brownian motion and does not allow for negative prices. We review a couple of simple models which allow for negative prices. They include the century-old Bachelier model and a model based on hyperbolic sine scaling of an arithmetic brownian motion. The latter has a dynamic close to the log-normal for large prices and similar to Bachelier for small prices.

title: A Framework for Regulating Programmable Digital Asset Markets

detail.title: A Framework for Regulating Programmable Digital Asset Markets

contentFormat.other: Summary Legislative Approach to Regulatory Regime

detail.abstract:
This is a summary version of a developing legislative proposal for the market structure for digital assets. The summary sets forth the critical failures of the current proposals as well as the fundamental construct of a proposed approach. The Fourth Industrial Revolution is shifting the foundation of capitalism from human institutions to algorithmic architecture. While trust has been enforced by courts, regulators, and intermediaries, it is now increasingly ensured by code. This transformation promises efficiency, but also redefines where risk lives—and who bears it.

Current U.S. digital asset legislation measures form instead of function — defining assets by name (“security,” “commodity,” and a proposed “ancillary asset”) rather than by the economic behaviors and risk exposures they generate. This proposal presents a Market Architecture of Trust, a structural framework for regulating digital asset markets through measurement, design, and proportionate intervention, rather than categorical overreach. The approach revives the principles of the 1903’s securities and derivatives laws—function over form, visibility as accountability—while updating them for programmable economies.

Regulatory intervention has been necessary when there is abstraction of ownership and control of economic interests/rights, which is more exacting in its analysis since those interests/rights are modularized or disaggregated from the previously inextricably combined bundles of rights. The central concept is to regulate residual risk, not form. Technology can internalize many governance functions once performed by law; regulation should scale only where residual risk—risk not neutralized by architecture—remains.

title: The Covenant Liquidity Index: A Framework for Rating Private Credit Liquidity and Secondary Market Discounts

detail.title: The Covenant Liquidity Index: A Framework for Rating Private Credit Liquidity and Secondary Market Discounts
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Covenant Liquidity Index (CLI), a quantitative framework for rating contractual liquidity in private credit and linking it to secondary-market discounting. Building on the theoretical foundation established in The Covenant Structure of Private Credit Yield (Saeidinezhad, 2025), the paper moves from theory to measurement. It argues that liquidity in private markets is not discovered through trading but engineered through covenant design—by defining when, how, and under what conditions capital can move. The CLI translates this design into a standardized score based
on three interlocking dimensions: exit engineering, cash-flow pacing, and optionality structuring. High-CLI instruments—those with deterministic exits, rule-based pacing, and bounded flexibility—exhibit lower secondary discount rates and tighter pricing dispersion; low-CLI structures trade at deeper discounts reflecting timing uncertainty. By quantifying how liquidity is manufactured ex ante and priced ex post, the CLI establishes a structural bridge between covenant architecture and valuation, providing the foundation for a Covenant Term Structure of Liquidity.

title: Time Compression in Economic Policy: Why Recoveries are Faster Today

detail.title: Time Compression in Economic Policy: Why Recoveries are Faster Today

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal relationships that could have influenced the research presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study does not involve human participants, interviews, or experimental data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support. It was completed as part of the author’s independent macroeconomic studies.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the concept of time compression in economic policy. Historically, governments and central banks responded slowly to crises, extending recessions and delaying recoveries. During the Great Depression of the 1930s, for instance, U.S. unemployment remained above 15 percent for much of the decade, and equity markets did not regain their 1929 peak until 1954 (Federal Reserve, 2020).

In contrast, the COVID-19 pandemic of 2020 saw governments deliver trillions of dollars in fiscal and monetary support within weeks, stabilizing markets at unprecedented speed (International Monetary Fund, 2021). Case studies from the United States, Canada, Europe, Japan, India, and China illustrate how rapid interventions have reshaped recovery timelines.

While accelerated action aids faster rebounds, it also introduces risks such as policy overshooting, volatility, and moral hazard. The paper concludes that time compression has not eliminated economic cycles but has changed their speed and intensity, creating windows of opportunity and risk that now open and close far more rapidly than in the past.

title: The Geography of a Persistent Divide: Stationarity of the Gender Unemployment Gap across Iran's Provinces
affiliations: Academic Center for Education, Culture and Research (ACECR), Academic Center for Education, Culture, and Research (ACECR), Tarbiat Modares University, Tehran, Iran and Alzahra University

detail.title: The Geography of a Persistent Divide: Stationarity of the Gender Unemployment Gap across Iran's Provinces
detail.abstract: This paper examines the persistence of the gender unemployment gap across Iran's 31 provinces from 2001Q2 to 2025Q1. It seeks to determine whether these regional labor market disparities are short-term fluctuations or structural and enduring features of provincial economies. By employing a range of unit root tests, our analysis reveals that the gender unemployment gap is largely persistent, with economic shocks exerting a long-lasting influence in most provinces. This stationarity indicates that the disparity is not a transient phenomenon but a deeply rooted structural characteristic of regional labor markets. These findings underscore the necessity for policymakers to design targeted, region-specific labor market strategies that address these entrenched inequalities.

title: Tools for Endogenous Monetary Policy Analysis: Optimal Projections and Instrument Rules
affiliations: Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England, Bank of England - Monetary Analysis, Bank of England, Bank of England and Bank of England

detail.title: Tools for Endogenous Monetary Policy Analysis: Optimal Projections and Instrument Rules

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of England Macro Technical Paper No. 4

detail.abstract: Optimal policy projections (OPPs) and simple instrument rules can be used to compare macroeconomic projections under different assumptions about monetary policy. This paper explains how both are used as inputs to the monetary policy process at the Bank of England. The underlying algorithms for endogenous policy analysis are flexible and can be applied to a range of macroeconomic models. Using a medium-scale DSGE model for the UK economy, we first explain the intuition underpinning the macroeconomic outcomes that OPPs and simple rules deliver. We then highlight the uses, as well as some challenges, of endogenous policy analysis in practice.

title: A General Theoretical Framework for Non-Equilibrium Plasma Dynamics: Integrating Gradient, Memory, Quantum, and Critical Phenomena

detail.title: A General Theoretical Framework for Non-Equilibrium Plasma Dynamics: Integrating Gradient, Memory, Quantum, and Critical Phenomena

publicationDetails.detailsText: This research addresses fundamental challenges in plasma physics by developing a unified theoretical framework that systematically incorporates four essential physical mechanisms neglected in conventional models.

detail.abstract: This research addresses fundamental challenges in plasma physics by developing a unified theoretical framework that systematically incorporates four essential physical mechanisms neglected in conventional models. We demonstrate that gradient-driven instabilities, non-Markovian memory effects, quantum correlations, and critical transition phenomena are indispensable for accurate description of strongly non-equilibrium plasmas. Through rigorous first-principles derivation and extensive validation across lightning phenomena (47 events), gas discharge systems, and laboratory plasmas, our integrated model achieves 92 % predictive accuracy, substantially outperforming conventional approaches (67 %). The framework provides physicallygrounded parameter estimation with comprehensive uncertainty quantification and establishes well-defined applicability boundaries.

title: Antifa- Networks of Protest and the Question of Legitimacy

detail.title: Antifa- Networks of Protest and the Question of Legitimacy
detail.abstract: This analysis explores the rise and operational dynamics of Antifa as a decentralized, ideologically driven network that leverages constitutional freedoms in democratic societies to foment unrest and weaken state institutions. While presenting itself as a movement against fascism, Antifa thrives in environments of weak leadership and limited accountability, employing both physical violence and digital intimidation to destabilize communities. Its loose organizational structure—lacking formal leadership or membership—renders it difficult to counter through conventional legal or political mechanisms. The movement’s influence is amplified by a broader ecosystem of funding and ideological support, including foundations, NGOs, and sympathetic political elites, which sustain and legitimize its disruptive activities. Comparative examples, including urban radicalism in India and Naxalism, demonstrate that these patterns of destabilization are not isolated but part of a global trend of leftist activism aimed at challenging sovereignty, delegitimizing institutions, and creating political chaos. The study positions strong, decisive governance as essential to maintaining social order in the face of such amorphous threats.

title: Don't Ruin the Surprise: Temporal Aggregation Bias in Structural Innovations

detail.title: Don't Ruin the Surprise: Temporal Aggregation Bias in Structural Innovations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no financial, professional, or personal relationships influencing this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) Insight Grant 435-2025-1423.

detail.abstract: Structural innovations estimated from temporally aggregated data (sums or averages) are shown to be mistimed. Selective sampling rectifies this bias only under specific conditions. We propose a method to test for temporal aggregation bias that reveals more than 70 percent of structural innovations occurred in previous months. Applying this test, we find significant mistiming in shocks to the global crude oil market and to monetary policy. Financial markets are shown to have already responded to the predictable component. This predictability and mistiming challenge the reliability of structural economic conclusions drawn from monthly or quarterly data.

title: Contingent Reasoning in Risky Choice

detail.title: Contingent Reasoning in Risky Choice
detail.abstract: Decisions under risk that stem from shared rather than mutually independent sources are ubiquitous in financial decision-making. In insurance choice, plans on the menu present positively correlated lotteries. This paper experimentally induces contingent reasoning in choice under risk. Using prize wheels to illustrate the correlation between lotteries, I vary whether subjects sequentially learn the outcomes of states or individual lotteries. Eye-tracking data reveal that experimental treatments altered evaluation procedures. I find causal evidence that statewise comparisons prompt more risk-averse choices. Implications are significant since insurance policy designers can extract surplus from consumers by emphasizing trade-offs between premiums and deductibles.

title: BKK Meets Romer: International Business Cycles in a Knowledge Economy
affiliations: , Hong Kong Baptist University and Michigan State University

detail.title: BKK Meets Romer: International Business Cycles in a Knowledge Economy
detail.abstract: Innovation, technology adoption, and international knowledge spillovers are key to understanding medium-run international business cycles. Empirically, we merge multi-country data on trade, patent stocks, and citation networks to document three key facts: (i) trade strengthens international GDP and TFP comovement; (ii) knowledge spillovers occur through trade and follow the global citation network; (iii) medium-run output fluctuations are driven mostly by the diffusion and adoption of technologies than by immediate innovations. We develop an international real business cycle model that embeds endogenous innovation, gradual technology adoption, and cross-border knowledge diffusion. Our quantitative model reveals that transitory trade shocks can lead to persistent GDP responses through their interaction with the endogenous dynamics of adoption and knowledge diffusion. These results show that innovation and diffusion dynamics amplify the transmission of transitory trade shocks, transforming them into persistent medium-run business cycle fluctuations.

title: The Long Road to Risk-Based Capital in India's Insurance Sector: A Historical and Strategic Overview

detail.title: The Long Road to Risk-Based Capital in India's Insurance Sector: A Historical and Strategic Overview
detail.abstract: Risk-Based Capital (RBC) has become the cornerstone of solvency supervision in insurance worldwide. Its purpose is to align regulatory capital requirements with the actual risk profile of insurers, thereby strengthening policyholder protection and financial stability. India's transition toward RBC has been a long-running reform project, spanning nearly two decades. Despite multiple committees, consultations, and pilot studies, the framework remains a workin-progress as of 2025. This article provides a comprehensive historical overview of the RBC journey in India-tracing its conceptual roots, policy milestones, challenges, and current implementation roadmap under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI). The discussion situates India's efforts within global RBC developments (Solvency II in Europe, the US RBC model, and emerging frameworks in Asia) and highlights the structural, operational, and cultural factors that have delayed full adoption. It concludes by outlining the likely contours of India's forthcoming regime and its implications for solvency, governance, and market discipline.

title: Safety as Justification: The Union Cycliste Internationale's Gear-Ratio Crackdown and the Bias Toward Restriction
affiliations: Victoria University of Wellington - Te Herenga Waka

detail.title: Safety as Justification: The Union Cycliste Internationale's Gear-Ratio Crackdown and the Bias Toward Restriction
detail.abstract: The Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) recently announced a ban on certain gear ratios in professional road racing, invoking “rider safety” as its principal rationale. A Belgian court subsequently issued an injunction suspending enforcement, finding the evidentiary basis for the rule unclear. This viewpoint argues that the UCI’s action exemplifies a broader behavioural tendency in sports regulation: a bias toward restriction in the absence of quantified trade-offs. Drawing on empirical literature in road safety and theoretical work on regulatory behaviour, I suggest that the UCI’s policy reflects a strong precautionary and performative form of governance, one that substitutes rhetorical safety claims for transparent, evidence-based analysis. Reframing "safety" as a discipline, rather than a slogan, would strengthen both legitimacy and effectiveness in sport regulation.

title: Treaty Entitlement, Principal Purpose Test, and GAAR-Select Issues

detail.title: Treaty Entitlement, Principal Purpose Test, and GAAR-Select Issues
detail.abstract:
The General Anti-Avoidance Rules have been on the statute in India for almost a decade. The court rulings relating to GAAR have started trickling in. The GAAR is no longer just for passive reading; it has entered the boardrooms, where decision-makers in business are actively seeking reassurance that commercial transactions do not fall foul of the general anti-avoidance rules.

It will be some years before the judicial examination of the provisions and their interpretation by the courts becomes available in sufficient quantity and scope as guidance to taxpayers and administrators. In this scenario, a close look at the statutory provisions in Chapter X-A, along with a scan of codified GAAR in other jurisdictions that have rich jurisprudence interpreting these provisions, may provide some insights into how the provisions will eventually be interpreted by the courts in India. This paper deals with some selected issues. It initiates discussion around them with a hope of gauging what the future holds for GAAR.

title: The Progressive Alliance and Its Global Footprint

detail.title: The Progressive Alliance and Its Global Footprint
detail.abstract: This study examines the evolution, structure, and influence of transnational progressive networks, emphasizing the Progressive Alliance as a contemporary manifestation of century-long ideological coordination. Tracing roots from the Fabian Society and the Socialist International, these networks have historically shaped political, economic, and cultural policies globally, often leveraging institutions, philanthropy, and media to advance agendas framed as equality, multiculturalism, and social justice. While publicly championed as universal ideals, their implementation frequently conflicts with populist-nationalist movements, revealing a systematic targeting of leaders defending sovereignty and cultural identity. Through coordinated alignment among political parties, think tanks, NGOs, and donors—including the United States’ Democratic Party and George Soros-backed foundations—the Progressive Alliance demonstrates a pattern of ideological influence that transcends borders, reminiscent of a modernized, institutionalized form of historical imperial control. India’s role as a strategic battleground is highlighted by recent meetings in Hyderabad, underscoring the country’s significance within this global contest of ideas. The study presents these developments not as conspiratorial speculation but as observable patterns in political history, institutional networks, and global coordination, suggesting that what is often dismissed as coincidence may reflect a deliberate, transnational strategy of ideological continuity.

title: The Central Bank as Safe Haven: evidence from interwar Spain

detail.title: The Central Bank as Safe Haven: evidence from interwar Spain
detail.abstract: Before becoming public institutions during the second half of the twentieth century, central banks acted as deposit taking institutions that interacted with the public, acting as a potential safe haven for bank deposits during financial crises. This paper tackles this historical relationship between banks and central banks by providing evidence on the behavior of central bank retail deposits vis-à-vis the rest of banks’ deposits in Spain during a bank run in 1931. I draw from annual panel data from the Banco de España’s network of branches and quarterly panel data for the universe of banks operating in Spain during the period. I exploit the exogenous shock to bank deposits caused by the unexpected proclamation of the Spanish Second Republic in April 1931, in order to test whether BdE retail deposits were used as a safe haven and whether a higher pre-crisis presence of the BdE amplified deposit withdrawals from banks. I complement this with data on daily new central bank deposit accounts opened and central bank lending operations at the individual level. I find evidence of a flight-to-safety from commercial bank deposits to BdE retail deposits in cities that experienced stronger bank runs and a permanent one in cities where a locally large bank failed. I also find that greater pre-crisis presence of the BdE retail deposit facility in the city amplified the impact of the political shock on bank deposits, thus highlighting the importance of the interplay between banks’ and central bank deposits in the historical development of banking systems.

title: Influence of Brand Personification on Consumer Behavior: A Study on Brand Loyalty and Decision-Making Based on Intermediary Regulation Model
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU), City University of Hong Kong (CityU), Hunan University of Finance and Economics and Mälardalen University

detail.title: Influence of Brand Personification on Consumer Behavior: A Study on Brand Loyalty and Decision-Making Based on Intermediary Regulation Model
detail.abstract: In order to explore the relationship and mechanism of brand personification on brand loyalty and consumer decision-making, 310 consumers with product experience in China were investigated by using brand personification scale, brand loyalty scale, consumer decision-making scale and consumer interaction scale. The results show that: (1) brand personification has a significant positive predictive effect on brand loyalty and consumer decision-making; (2) Consumer interaction plays an intermediary role in the relationship between brand personification and brand loyalty, and between brand personification and consumer decision-making; (3) Consumer type and product type (search type/experience type) adjust the intermediary path through which brand personification affects brand loyalty and consumer decision-making through consumer interaction. Specifically, the mediating effect of consumer interaction between brand personification and brand loyalty, brand personification and consumer decision-making is more prominent when the scores of consumer type and product type are higher than those of consumer type and product type. The research results are helpful to reveal the internal mechanism of brand personification affecting brand loyalty and consumer decision-making, and have certain enlightenment significance for enterprises to formulate differentiated brand personification marketing strategies.

title: Beyond Epistemology: Noesology and the Rethinking of Intelligence

detail.title: Beyond Epistemology: Noesology and the Rethinking of Intelligence
detail.abstract: The evolving landscape of intelligence research necessitates a paradigm shift beyond conventional epistemological frameworks. Traditional cognitive models, rooted in reductionist perspectives, have struggled to encapsulate the complexity of intelligence, consciousness, and knowledge production in an increasingly interconnected world. This paper introduces Noesology, a transdisciplinary epistemological framework that integrates insights from cognitive science, artificial intelligence (AI), philosophy, neuroscience, and complexity theory to redefine intelligence as a multi-layered, dynamic, and emergent phenomenon. Noesology, derived from the Greek noein (νοεῖν), meaning "to perceive by the intellect," and logos (λόγος), meaning "study" or "discourse," provides a novel perspective on knowledge by emphasizing embodiment, collective intelligence, transdisciplinary integration, and systems thinking. It critically evaluates the limitations of traditional epistemologies, including Cartesian dualism, Kantian transcendental idealism, and cognitive reductionism, arguing that intelligence is best understood as an emergent and systemic phenomenon that transcends anthropocentric biases. This study highlights the interconnections between natural, artificial, and collective intelligence, advocating for an epistemological framework that integrates ecological intelligence, indigenous knowledge systems, and the ethical implications of AI. Through a comprehensive literature review and empirical case studies, this paper demonstrates the applicability of Noesology in education, AI development, social sciences, and ecological sustainability. It ultimately proposes a new model of intelligence—one that reflects the complexity, interconnectivity, and dynamic nature of knowledge production in the 21st century. The research concludes by discussing the practical implications of Noesology for rethinking pedagogy, fostering ethical AI development, enhancing collective intelligence in governance, and promoting ecological sustainability. By advancing a transdisciplinary epistemology, this paper contributes to the ongoing discourse on intelligence, emphasizing the need for a holistic, integrative, and future-oriented approach to knowledge and cognition.
